text: Infrastructure as code, automated deployment, and service monitoring
A proposed delivery design for the GearFlow garage management platform
GearFlow today and the deployment gap
The codebase already has a web app and API. The infrastructure automation below is a proposed extension.
React 18 + Vite frontend; Axios calls the /api routes
Spring Boot 3 REST API with role-based JWT security
MySQL persistence through Spring Data JPA
No Terraform, Ansible, CI pipeline, or Nagios config is present today
Package the React build and Spring Boot JAR as release artifacts
Provision hosts/network with Terraform; configure and deploy with Ansible
Add health endpoints and Nagios checks before production rollout
This deck describes a deployment design to implement; it does not claim these tools are already embedded in GearFlow.
Release flow connects code to operations
One release artifact moves through tested, repeatable deployment steps.
gearflow-frontend/dist  +  gearflow-backend JAR  +  version and checksum
Tests pass  →  deployment approval  →  health checks pass  →  monitor release
Keep production topology small at first and expand only when traffic and availability needs justify it.

Spring Boot Actuator is not currently a dependency in the repository. Add and secure it before relying on /actuator/health.
Environment separation protects releases and data
Keep operational credentials outside source control and limit each layer to the access it needs.
Terraform state: remote storage, locking, restricted access
Ansible secrets: encrypted vault or managed secret service
CI credentials: least privilege and rotation
Database: private network path; no public MySQL port
Application: non-root service account and protected config
Operations: audit deployments and keep rollback artifacts
The database password and JWT signing key must move from application.properties into environment-specific secrets.
A staged rollout reduces deployment risk
Start with repeatable delivery in staging, then promote after measurable checks pass.
Document versioned frontend and backend build outputs.
Create dev/stage hosts and private network rules with Terraform.
Deploy the same release using Ansible roles and inventories.
Add Actuator health endpoint and Nagios host/service checks.
Run smoke tests, approve production, and rehearse rollback.
Repeatable deploy  •  verified health  •  private database  •  tested rollback
